artifact: opy-rs OverPy feature inventory and support matrix

snapshot.note: Evidence-base snapshot (issue #2). No opy-rs frontend implementation is merged on main yet (issues #3-#7), so states are current-repository states, not target states: frontend-surface features are `planned` until the frontend workstream lands corpus-evidenced behavior, and features whose completion requires canonical Workshop semantics are `lowering-dependent` and inventory-only until the workshop-rs integration stage (#8).

states.planned: Declared surface, not yet implemented in opy-rs; evidence/provenance recorded for the implementing issue.
states.frontend-supported: Frontend behavior (lex/parse/preprocess/macro expansion) implemented in opy-rs and corpus-evidenced.
states.semantic-supported: Semantic resolution implemented in opy-rs (names, members, enums, call semantics covered by the semantic model).
states.lowering-dependent: Completion requires canonical Workshop semantics/catalog/emission owned by workshop-rs; inventory-only until the integration stage.
states.end-to-end-supported: Full OPY to Workshop compile parity through the workshop-rs integration boundary.

features.name: Lexer: identifiers, literals, strings, comments, #! directives, operators
features.notes: Issue #3. Rejected sub-forms (dict literals, triple-quoted strings, backslash continuation, postfix ++/--) must fail with explicit diagnostics; baseline category 1.

features.name: Expression/postfix/member/call grammar, precedence, indexing
features.notes: Issue #3. Corpus subset is baseline-supported in the declared contract; `del`/`in`/`not in` stay out (see syntax/switch).

features.name: Declarations: globalvar/playervar (index + initializer), subroutine, def, enum, macro constants
features.notes: Issues #3/#4. Bare-integer index form is an explicit Workshop variable index; integer-0 initializers are dropped from HIR matching the reference; Initialize-rule synthesis is lowering-dependent.

features.name: Assignments and control flow: =, augmented ops, if/elif/else, for-in-range, while, pass
features.notes: Issue #3. Baseline category 3; augmented operators include min=/max= per the reference.

features.name: switch/case/default, do…while, hex 0x literals, expression-level not in
features.notes: Baseline category 1a: evidence-prioritized. Explicitly rejected (documented diagnostics) until implemented.

features.name: String modifiers (f/w/l/b/c/t), dict literals, list comprehensions, lambda
features.notes: Baseline category 1b: legacy-quirk/demand-driven for dicts and modifiers, evidence-prioritized for comprehensions; explicit rejection until demand is demonstrated.

features.name: settings { ... } custom-game-settings blocks: JSONC parse into the typed HIR payload
features.notes: Issue #3. Parsing/placement validation is frontend-owned; the Workshop settings-section emission is lowering-dependent (see semantics/settings-emission).

features.name: Name resolution: undeclared identifiers, subroutine and constant references, enum types
features.notes: Issue #4. Structured source-located diagnostics: unknown-identifier, enum-type-without-member, unsupported-member.

features.name: for-loop binder: declared globalvar or implicit default variables A-Z … DA-DX
features.notes: Issue #4. Agent-lab regression: undeclared uppercase binder is an implicit global at its fixed Workshop slot; nested same-name loops reuse the binding; lowercase undeclared binders rejected like the reference.

features.name: Builtin actions and values (manifest-declared surface; full 225 action / 267 value Workshop surface)
features.notes: Issue #4. Resolves through the opy-rs semantic compatibility manifest (crates/wright-opy/src/manifest/, spec: docs/opy/compat-manifest-spec.md); every entry probe-validated against the pinned oracle. Full surface stays baseline-planned.

features.name: Receiver/member functions: receiver categories, explicit-argument signatures, variable receivers
features.notes: Issue #4. Includes the bare-playervar-receiver residual item (A = B.C, baseline-planned). Workshop emission of member calls through the catalog is lowering-dependent.

features.name: Builtin enum/constant domains and members (declared domains; 46 upstream domains incl. Hero/Map/Gamemode)
features.notes: Issue #4. Members outside declared domains fail with unknown-enum-member (Color.CYAN, DynamicEffect.SPARKLES …); full domain surface stays baseline-planned; emission spellings are lowering-dependent.

features.name: Source aliases: non-contextual (stopChasingVariable, getCurrentHero, hasStatusEffect) and the ChaseReeval contextual alias
features.notes: Issue #4/#5. Remaining alias surface (hero renames, obsolete names) stays legacy-quirk/demand-driven; ChaseReeval resolves only in the chase call context.

features.name: Modules: random.{randint,uniform,choice,shuffle}
features.notes: Issue #4. Corpus-evidenced: random.uniform/random.choice; range/random.*/.format route around the reference's generic keyword binder (keyword-unsupported).

features.name: Named/keyword arguments: generic name=expr binding and the chase/ChaseReeval special form
features.notes: Issue #4. raycast include=/exclude= and macro keyword arguments stay evidence-prioritized (no corpus/reference evidence in the declared surface).

features.name: Source identity and diagnostics: structured, source-located frontend errors, wright-result/v1 envelope
features.notes: Issues #3/#4. Stable codes (lex-error, parse-error, unknown-*, invalid-*, enum-*, chase-*); parser recovers at statement boundaries; S/D evidence class.

features.name: Workshop settings-section emission: key table, enum values, map/hero list elements
features.notes: The typed settings payload is frontend-owned; the emission table and its domains are Workshop data owned by workshop-rs. Emitted settings are deliberately not reparseable (round-trip boundary).

features.name: #!include: root-relative resolution, cycle detection, missing-file diagnostics, file registry
features.notes: Issue #5. Real-world fixtures are full include closures (per-file SHA-256 recorded in fixture.json).

features.name: #!define (object- and function-like), #!undef, recursive expansion, recursion guard
features.notes: Issue #5. Unsupported directives fail explicitly (unsupported-directive); macro-recursion guard.

features.name: #!mainFile, #!allowMacroRedeclaration, #!optimize*/#!replace0By* family, #!rulePrefix*
features.notes: Baseline category 5a: legacy-quirk/demand-driven; explicit rejection until the declared compatibility target requires them.

features.name: macro name(params): statement bodies with MacroParam references, macro constants
features.notes: Issue #5. Macro keyword arguments are treated as raw text by the reference and rejected explicitly.

features.name: __script__ JavaScript macros and post-compile hooks (QuickJS runtime)
features.notes: Issue #6. Bounded runtime compatibility surface; does not require Node.js compatibility (issue #1); the reference's quickjs-ng.wasm is pinned in the oracle package.

features.name: Rule annotations: @Event, @Condition, bare @Team/@Slot; evidence-prioritized: @Team/@Slot args, @Name, @Hero, @Disabled, @Delimiter, @NewPage, @SuppressWarnings
features.notes: Issue #3/#5. Baseline categories 4 (bare forms) and 4a (argument forms, evidence-prioritized); other @ directives fail explicitly.

features.name: Rule model: rule "name": with events (global, eachPlayer), conditions list, statements
features.notes: Issue #3. Rule disabled markers stay out (no corpus evidence for the source annotation).

features.name: #!translations directive recognition and .po generation surface
features.notes: Baseline category 5a: legacy-quirk/demand-driven; directive recognition is frontend-owned; the emitted locale data path is lowering-dependent.

features.name: Localized Workshop output (--language flag, localizedStrings data)
evidence: oracle:CLI --language en-US invocation recorded in compatibility/run_oracle.py
features.notes: Locale data is Workshop-owned content (workshop-rs); the oracle harness pins en-US as the evidence language.

features.name: #!optimize*/#!replace0By* family and compression controls
features.notes: Baseline category 5a: legacy-quirk/demand-driven. Optimizer choices are not a compatibility contract; only observable semantics count.

features.name: Workshop text emission form (variable naming, enum spellings, formatting)
features.notes: Output-text identity is explicitly not the compatibility contract; exact-vs-normalized differences are presentation differences. Emission form is workshop-rs-owned.

features.name: QuickJS runtime for __script__ hook execution
evidence: oracle:quickjs-ng.wasm shipped in the pinned npm package
features.notes: Issue #6. Bounded runtime surface: reference-compatible accept/reject and result semantics for documented hook probes; no Node.js compatibility required.

features.name: Frontend pipeline: lexer -> preprocess -> CST/parser -> semantic resolution -> Opy HIR v1
features.notes: Issues #3-#5. Fully Workshop-independent; the whole corpus is the target acceptance corpus; differential HIR parity is issue #7.

features.name: HIR -> Workshop lowering and emission through workshop-rs
features.notes: Issue #8; blocked on the workshop-rs public contracts (wrightkit/workshop-rs#2). Oracle snapshots (fixtures/**/oracle.json) remain the reference; no temporary Workshop IR is introduced here.

features.name: End-to-end OPY -> Workshop compile parity
features.notes: Becomes end-to-end-supported only after the workshop-rs integration stage (#8); differential harness contract is ready (compatibility/diff.py, issue #7 wiring).

features.name: Workshop -> OPY decompilation
features.notes: Deferred until the canonical Workshop semantic representation exists (workshop-rs integration); a non-goal before it. Upstream decompiler corpus (17 inputs) is the future reference.

features.name: Round-trip boundary: emitted settings reparsing, .ws round-trip
features.notes: Documented boundary: emitted settings sections are deliberately not reparseable; a .ws decompiler is a non-goal. Reconstruction of arbitrary Workshop text is out of scope.
